primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Three components, trained end-to-end: (a) **Transformer encoder** (3 layers, 8 attention heads per layer, model dimension 256; causal mask to prevent future access) maps the full motion sequence x_{0:T-1} ∈ R^{T×45} to K=12

primitives.name: Neural ODE Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: (b) **Neural ODE**: from z_0, the latent trajectory is generated by integrating dẑ(t)/dt = f_θ(z(t), t), where f_θ is a 3-layer MLP (two hidden layers × 128 units, tanh activations) defining a vector field on the latent space; deterministic flow, trajectory length T matched to the original sequence.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'z(t)': 'latent trajectory in 3D space, meters', 'f_θ': 'vector field defined by 3-layer MLP, dimensionless', 't': 'time variable, seconds'}
primitives.assumptions: Deterministic flow; vector field approximated by MLP with tanh activation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure under non-stationary or chaotic regimes without sufficient training data.

layer2.mapping: Generates continuous latent trajectories from discrete initial conditions using learned vector fields.
layer2.telemetry: Trajectory reconstruction accuracy and phase-space consistency.

primitives.name: MLP Decoder
primitives.verbatim_quote: (c) **MLP decoder** (3 fully connected layers, two hidden layers × 256 units ReLU, linear output) reconstructs the 45-D joint positions from the predicted latent trajectory.

primitives.assumptions: Linear output layer ensures direct mapping from latent to spatial coordinates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when latent space lacks sufficient discriminative power for accurate decoding.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology combines a Transformer-based encoder to embed full-body motion sequences into a low-dimensional latent space, followed by a Neural Ordinary Differential Equation (NODE) that evolves these latent states deterministically over time. This architecture allows prediction of complete motion from only an initial segment (~8%) by leveraging the learned dynamical flow. The decoder then translates the predicted latent trajectory back into physical joint positions. The system assumes deterministic dynamics and uses causal masking during encoding to avoid information leakage. Key limitations include lack of interpretability of latent variables, absence of uncertainty quantification, and limited generalization due to subject-specific training. The method demonstrates moderate performance (R² ≈ 0.46) but fails to capture complex ecological variability present in real-world sports contexts such as NFL tracking data.
